[2022]</ref>.3 PreliminariesGeneral-sum Markov Games. We consider an episodic time-inhomogeneous general-sum Markov game M, consisting of m players, a shared state space S, an individual action space A i for each player i ∈ [m] and a joint action space A = A 1 × A 2 × • • • A m . The game has a time horizon H, an initial state s 1 , state transition probabilities P = (P 1 , P 2 , • • • , P H ) with P h : SA → ∆(S), and rewards R = R h (• | s h , a h ) H h=1 where R h,i ∈ [0, 1] represents the random reward for player i at step h. At each step h ∈ [H], all players observe current state s h and simultaneously choose their actions a h = (a h,1 , a h,2 , • • • , a h,m ). The next state s h+1 is then sampled from P h (• | s h , a h ), and the reward r h,i for player i is sampled from R h,i (• | s h , a h ). The game terminates at step H + 1, with each player aiming to maximize the total collected rewards.
